about: The frigate's boats (docs/shipkit-11): a launch, two cutters and a gig on spare spars over the open waist, the stream anchor and the large kedge across the launch, the small kedge across the port cutter. Each hull is lofted from a period draught's traced lines (lines, feet in the draught's frame) scaled to the boat (boats), planked (carvel or clinker), framed and fitted out; stowage places them on cradles across their spars, which lie on saddles on the waist's beams, the gig nested in the starboard cutter, each griped down. Metres in the ship's frame (X forward, Y starboard, Z up, origin on the centreline at midships on waterline A) unless a key says ft or in. Every size is the period's practice for a 44's boats (an estimate) unless its src gives a source.

sources.longboat_1801: Royal Museums Greenwich J0267, '31ft Longboat (circa 1801)', a public domain scan on Wikimedia Commons: profile, half-breadth plan and body plan, 'A Longboat. Dimensions: Length 31 ft 0 in, Breadth Moulded 9 ft 6 in, Depth Midship 4 ft 1 in' written on it, with her thwarts, windlass, mast steps, stern sheets, sling plates and the roller in her stem head. Measured only (lines.longboat_1801): the scan is not in the repository
sources.pinnace_1840: Royal Museums Greenwich J0667, 'Draught of a Pinnace' (signed J. W., 6 February 1840; traced 1951), a public domain scan on Wikimedia Commons: 'Length 30 ft 0 in, Breadth 8 ft 7 in, Depth 3 ft 1 in', profile with the washstrake and six rowlock notches a side, half-breadth plan, body plan. Measured only (lines.pinnace_1840)
sources.juste_launch_1794: Royal Museums Greenwich J0022, '27ft armed launch for Juste (1794)', a public domain scan on Wikimedia Commons: a launch of the 1790s (her stern sheets, thwarts and knees by eye)
sources.inventory: USS Constitution's boats as listed by the U.S. Navy and others (as quoted by the searches; the pages themselves are on hosts this machine cannot open): a 36 ft longboat, two 30 ft cutters, two 28 ft whaleboats, a 28 ft gig, a 22 ft jolly boat and a 14 ft punt, her later outfit. The plan (docs/shipkit-0) carries four for 1797: a launch, two cutters and a small gig
sources.anchors: anchors_1797.json: the stream anchor (1,100 lb) and the two kedges (700 and 400 lb) stow with the boats (Bean's choice, Nov 15), the launch carrying them out to kedge
sources.waist: deck_1797.json and deck.py: the open waist 43 ft 8 in long between the breaks and 23 ft 4 in between the coamings, seven beams across it (14 by 10 in, their tops 3 in under the deck's top), the ladders down to the gun deck either side of the middle line at each break
sources.practice: the period's practice for a frigate's boats, by eye where no draught gives it (each so marked)

longboat_1801.frame: feet in the draught's own frame: x forward from the stern post's aft edge at the transom's top (the post's aft edge runs down and forward from there to the keel), y the half-breadth, z up from the base (the keel's rabbet amidships). The lines are moulded (inside the planking: 'Breadth Moulded' is written on the draught). Each station's yz runs from the rabbet up to the sheer at the centre of the ink; the transom edge (x, y, z) from its heel on the post to its top corner; the sheer and the stem's lines are the profile's (x, z), the gunwale the half-breadth plan's (x, y). The stations drawn red (No 1-3 aft, A-D forward) are cant frames: their lines in the plan cross the middle line at x and run aft or forward going outboard, cant the tangent of that (forward if positive, fitted to the red ink); the body plan draws them in their true shape, so their yz is the distance out along the cant line and the height
longboat_1801.post_note: the post's aft edge from the transom's top (x 0, z 5.48) down to the keel (x 1.12, z 0.03): the transom's outer face lies in the plane through it, square to the middle line

fittings.note: read off the draught's profile and plan (feet, its frame), each scaled with the hull
fittings.src: the thwarts' ends, the mast steps and partners, the windlass's bitts and barrel, the stern sheets' rail, the sling plates on her side and the roller in her stem head as drawn; the bottom boards' top from the red line in her profile amidships

pinnace_1840.frame: feet in the draught's own frame, as the longboat's: x forward from the transom's aft face at its top, y the half-breadth, z up from the base (the keel's rabbet amidships); moulded lines. Five stations; the run aft of station 2 and the entrance forward of B are drawn by the two waterlines (blue in the plan, at their heights z from the body plan's blue lines, each from the post or deadwood to the stem), the transom, the sheer, the gunwale in plan and the stem's rabbet. The washstrake (6 in deep, six rowlock notches a side) stands on the sheer (washstrake_top, traced from x 10.8 forward); the rubbing strake's top line is traced too

fittings.note: read off the draught's profile (feet, its frame)
fittings.src: the thwarts (red) about 8 in under the sheer; the washstrake (traced as washstrake_top) about 6 in deep, its rowlock notches about 4 in wide and 2 in deep

launch.scale_src: practice: a 34 ft launch, the longboat's lines scaled alike every way (breadth moulded 10 ft 5 in, depth 4 ft 6 in); the inventory's 36 ft longboat is her later outfit's, and a 34 ft launch leaves the cutters room either side of her over the waist
launch.src: lines: the longboat's draught; build, frames and fittings practice for a launch of the period
launch.fit_src: practice: the capping as wide as the sheer strake, the timbers' heads and the inwale with a lip outside; hog_in the hog's moulding inside the rabbet; quarter knees and breasthook (arm or length, depth) under the cappings; the stern bench (stern_bench_in wide) round the stern sheets; thole pins in pairs (thole_gap_in apart) on the capping, rowlock_aft_in aft of each thwart's after edge; the masts' diameters the draught's partners; sails furled on their yards to a roll sail_roll_in thick; the painter coiled turns deep

cutter.scale_src: practice: 26 ft by 7 ft 3 in moulded, depth 2 ft 8 in, the pinnace's lines scaled (her breadth over the draught's greatest as traced, 8.57 ft); a cutter of the period was clinker built, a little finer than a pinnace
cutter.src: lines: the pinnace's draught (its washstrake and notches); build practice
cutter.fit_src: practice, as the launch's; thwart i (from 0 aft) at stern_sheets_ft + (i + first_thwart_room) thwart_room_ft, the masts stepped through mast_thwarts (indices), the bottom boards' top bottom_boards_z_ft above the base and the stern sheets' stern_sheets_below_sheer_ft under the sheer; the washstrake (washstrake_thick_in) on the capping, its notches over each rowlock

gig.scale_src: practice: a small gig 22 ft by 4 ft 10 in moulded, depth 1 ft 11 in (long and narrow, pulling four oars single banked), the pinnace's lines scaled (her breadth over the draught's greatest as traced, 8.57 ft)
gig.src: lines: the pinnace's draught, narrowed; build practice for a gig
gig.fit_src: practice, as the cutter's; single banked, her rowlocks alternating side to side (the stroke oar to port)

stowage.note: how the boats ride on the booms over the open waist (practice: the period stowed its boats on the spare spars laid fore and aft across the waist's beams, the launch in the middle and the other boats beside her or in her; deck_1797.json's waist note: the spar deck is named for them). Each spare spar rests on a saddle on every beam it crosses (the beams follow the deck's sheer, the spar is straight: each saddle at least saddle_min_in thick, its top hollowed to the spar); each boat sits level on two cradles laid across her spars under her straight keel, their tops cut to her outside (her keel in a slot, the lands of a clinker boat notched), and is griped down to the cradles' ends by two gripes over her gunwales. The ladders at each break keep their headroom and the gangways their clear width (checked: boats_room). Metres in the ship's frame
stowage.spars_src: spares the period carried on the booms (spars_1795.json's sizes, each built as the rig builds it: a yard's diameter diam_in_per_yard of its length in yards, its cleats; the mizzen topgallant mast with its royal pole, 23.3 + 12.1 ft; a topmast studding sail boom half its topsail yard, 1 in of diameter for each 5 ft), those that fit the waist's 43 ft 8 in opening between its breast beams: the topmasts, topsail yards, the jib boom and the main and fore topgallant masts with their poles (47 and 45 ft) are longer than it
stowage.saddle_note: a saddle as long as the beam is sided, a spar's diameter wide and saddle_wider_in more, its top hollowed to the spar: one shape its whole length, the lowest of the spar's undersides over it (a spare mast's square heel seated in a square channel), over 50 deg either side of its bottom
stowage.boats_note: each boat's spars as (name, y off her middle line, m); the cutters as close to the launch as gap_between_boats_in allows at every height (side: starboard 1, port -1)
stowage.x_mid: the waist's middle: every boat centred on it fore and aft

cradle.note: two cradles a boat, at these fractions of her straight keel (between the deadwood's foot and the forefoot), each across her two spars, its ends beyond them

stowage.nest_note: the gig on two chocks across the starboard cutter's thwarts (on_thwarts: their indices from aft), her keel in their slots, both boats griped together: each chock nest_chock_in fore and aft and under her keel, its ends where her bottom has risen chock_rise_in over her keel; the gig clear of everything in the cutter by nest_clear_in

gripes.note: a gripe at each cradle, from an eyebolt in one end up her side and over her gunwales (and whatever rides in her) to an eyebolt in the other, set up taut: it lies on the outline of what it passes over (their section's convex hull at the cradle), each end spliced round its eyebolt's eye (eye_in: the eye's centre-line diameter, its bar, the shank; into_in driven into the cradle's end), as anchors.py splices the shank painter, its end laid tail_gap_in clear of the standing part (one rope, so it must not touch itself); turned round each corner of the outline on its own radius and a hair (a rope bent round an edge)

anchors.note: each anchor's stock lies across her gunwales near one end, on their tops (the cappings, or a cutter's washstrakes), where her breadth over the cappings is the stock's length less stock_overhang_in each side, or as near there as lets it lie clear of her thole pins and what lies in her; its shank along her middle line toward her middle, the arms upright under it: turned down about the stock until the crown, an arm or the shank (never the stock) first rests on something in her (a thwart, the bottom boards, the anchor stowed before it)

stowage.budget_note: the plan's figure for slice 11 (the boats, their gear, the spares, saddles, cradles, chocks, gripes and the three anchors): a starting point, not a ceiling (Bean, Nov 12), so the build reports the count against it and never fails on it

meets.note: the stowage's objects against the ship and each other (boats_room, deck.room): the pairs whose surfaces meet by design and how deep (in) they may go into each other there; any other pair must stay clear (the gig of the cutter she nests in too)
pairs: each saddle on its beam's top
each saddle's top hollowed to its spar
each cradle notched over its boat's two spars
each cradle's top cut to her outside (straight between its faces, so a clinker land crossing it goes in a little)
the gig's chocks on the cutter's thwarts, cut to the gig's outside
each gripe's eyebolts driven into its cradle's ends
each gripe lying on what it passes over (its centre line its radius and 0.05 in off their outline: touching, never into them)
the stock on her cappings, the anchor resting in her
the stock on her cappings, the anchor resting in her

stowage.checks_note: boats_room: the boats, spars, saddles, cradles and gripes against the whole ship (and each other, the meetings by design in meets); the gangways' clear width under the boats (to headroom height above the gangway's deck); the ladders' headroom over every tread; the gig clear of the cutter she nests in

meets.note: inside each boat: the parts whose surfaces meet by design, and how deep (in) the two may go into each other there (Boat.room_check: every closed piece of one part tested inside the other's, at its corners and over its faces where the two cross, however deep; the allowance a quarter inch over the deepest measured in any of the three boats). Any other two parts must stay clear, and so must two pieces of one part (two frames, two oars) unless 'within' names that part

paint.src: practice: painted as the ship (black, an ochre band along the sheer strake, red inside), the thwarts, gunwales and stern sheets bright, the oars and spars oiled
